messages:
alice_support: starting thread for customer (BetaCorp). They report users seeing mid-stream disconnects when moving between carrier data and home WiFi. Client shows truncated generation and no final delimiter. Happening intermittently (~10-40s after handoff).

alice_support: case 110214. Customer attached app logs, small pcap and reproduction notes.

bob_oncall: can you paste a short log excerpt? need to see if it's TCP-level close or app-initiated.

alice_support: log excerpt below from their iOS app: 
```
[2026-07-02T18:05:02Z] SSE open /v1/streams session=b987
[2026-07-02T18:05:20Z] NETWORK: cellular->wifi handover
[2026-07-02T18:05:22Z] AUTH: refresh token start (ttl=45s)
[2026-07-02T18:05:23Z] AUTH: refresh -> 403 Forbidden
[2026-07-02T18:05:23Z] APP: client lib emits Close() and tears socket
[2026-07-02T18:05:23Z] STREAM: partial event chunk received, no done marker
```

charlie_runtime: 403 on refresh is interesting (not 401). Could be auth service throttling or a policy check failing during the handoff. If client closes the socket on any non-2xx refresh response, that explains truncation. Also note server may have already emitted tokens which are billable.

dave_mobile_client: I reproduced on local Android with emulator. Steps:
1) open SSE to /v1/streams using SDK v2.0.1 with short TTL tokens (45s)
2) trigger network switch (use emulator network toggle)
3) client hits refresh endpoint; when auth returns 4xx, the SDK immediately tears down SSE instead of retrying

I ran a curl-style repro to simulate invalidation: 
```
TOKEN=short
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?session=test"
# then flip auth server to return 403 for one request
```

elaine_sre: tagging runtime + billing. @charlie_runtime can runtime emit a resumable-id header (x-resume-id) at stream start so clients that reconnect can resume instead of losing progress? Also consider allowing a small window where refresh endpoint 4xx -> treated as transient if SSE connection still active.

charlie_runtime: proposed options:
- Add x-resume-id header in initial 200 response; store minimal resume state for N seconds.
- Implement tolerant-refresh mode: if auth refresh fails with 401/403 within a short grace (<=2s) while the original SSE TCP connection is still established, return 200 and allow the stream to continue.
- Emit periodic keepalive comments every 12s for flaky mobile slices to prevent client libs thinking connection stale.

bob_oncall: short-term mitigation for customers:
- Increase token TTL to 120s for mobile clients (avoids tight refresh windows during handoff)
- Update mobile SDK to treat single 4xx during refresh as retryable once with jitter

alice_support: customer is worried about billing: they saw several small charges tied to aborted streams during a test. Are tokens billed as soon as they are emitted by model?

billing-bot: FYI billing policy: tokens generated by the model are billed when produced. Aborted connections do not automatically undo charges. For suspected systemic issues, open billing review ticket with case ID.

elaine_sre: billing follow-up: I'll run an audit on case 110214 for repeated aborted-stream charges in the last 7 days and flag potential credits if refunds are warranted.

dave_mobile_client: I'll prepare an SDK patch that:
- refreshes proactively at 60% of TTL instead of waiting until last moment
- on refresh 4xx, performs a single retry with exponential backoff before closing SSE
- supports x-resume-id to reattach and request missing output ranges
ETA: staging build today, rollout next week.

charlie_runtime: runtime tasks:
- canary: x-resume-id header + keepalive comments on mobile route (deploy id: canary-2026-07-02-11)
- implement tolerant-refresh path for 2s grace window

elaine_sre: operations tasks:
- SRE will monitor auth backend 4xx/5xx spike during canary window; if increase >2x baseline, rollback
- request full pcap from customer and confirm TTL and SDK version (alice)

alice_support: requested pcap and SDK info. Customer replied: SDK v2.0.1, token TTL=45s, reproduces on iOS 16.4. They will provide full pcap later today.

bob_oncall: summary/action items:
- Support (alice): collect pcap, app logs, timeline
- Runtime (charlie): implement x-resume-id + tolerant-refresh canary
- Client (dave): SDK patch for proactive refresh + retry + resume support
- Billing (elaine): audit charges and prepare credits if systemic

alice_support: will keep customer posted and paste pcap when received. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
